items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: he joined me when I was going to make a tour, my first tour

ctx.x: I always try to think if he was given a nickname. I can't recall, because if you've ever played in Fletcher's band, they always give you a name. Somebody gives you a nickname. Whether you like it or not, you accept it eventually. I can't think what Jonah was called, but nevertheless Jonah is originally from Louisville, Kentucky, and he wasn't in my Wilberforce band, but he joined me when I was going to make a tour, my first tour, and he was always an excellent reader. He could play first, second or third, and he…

And we traveled quite a bit. I had a cousin of his named Russell Bowles, a trombone player that was one of the section men in the great Jimmie Lunceford band, and Russell was related to him, Jonah Jones, and Jonah got him in the

items.title: 68728_Jonah
items.q: And that was the trumpet section of Horace Henderson's band. And so he left, Red left, Red Holland left, and then they sent for me. So I come into the band

ctx.x: Matthew was a trumpet player that played around here with Charlie Johnson and different bands, you know.

And then he finally dropped out of sight. I don't know what happened to him. I used to see him years ago. He left Horace, and then let's see, had him, and this guy I told you, Bernice Morton, and Roy. And that was the trumpet section of Horace Henderson's band. And so he left, Red left, Red Holland left, and then they sent for me. So I come into the band and then there was me and Bernice Morton and Roy.
Well, that was your second professional job.
